input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second Section 12.4 binds Customer (not Vendor) with a post-term non-compete of 24 months, undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor") and unlimited territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions — indeed acquisitions are expressly barred. That is walk-away territory under the rule and well beyond the fallback (named competing product, term only, 12 months, internal-development/acquisition carve-outs). It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. We propose deleting 12.4 and relying on 12.3; a narrowed fallback restriction can be discussed if Vendor identifies a specific product needing protection.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we may build, buy, or resell, so we have deleted this 24-month, unlimited-territory non-compete, which also directly contradicts Section 12.3. If Cobalt needs protection for a specific offering, we can discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the Customer non-compete in the second Section 12.4.
